title: A quarter-sign test finds season terms in corrected KIC 10001893 flux but not in aperture flux at 14.261300 microHz
abstract: We test whether the known 19.48-hour signal of KIC 10001893 has repeated quarter-season terms after a common linear time drift. We reuse 51679 exposures from 14 public Kepler release 25 quarters. At a fixed prior frequency of 14.261300 microHz, a fitted-residual quarter-sign test gives tail fractions of 0.0090 and 0.0054 in corrected flux for 3-day and 6-day trends. Aperture flux gives 0.1490 and 0.2618. The paired flux difference gives 0.1479 and 0.0347, so it does not establish a stable processing effect. Specific 30 ppm season injections pass the reference screen at all 16 phases in both products. The sign test is conditional on residual symmetry, quarter independence, frequency and model choice. It is not an exact significance test. Both products share exposures. No planet, source location or physical cause is confirmed. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Fitted season amplitudes at a fixed known frequency, with common linear time drift. Lines join model coefficients, not times. Tail fractions are conditional residual-sign diagnostics. Products share observations. Vertical scales differ.
